newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PEASANTS SAY MAY TRY TO OUST PRIME MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PEASANTS SAY MAY TRY TO OUST PRIME MINISTER.

text.p: Just weeks before Poland's general election the co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL) threatened to press for dismissing Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz unless the cabinet agrees to the group's farming policy demands.

The Peasants said on Tuesday they would seek to oust Cimoszewicz of the ruling coalition's stronger party, the ex-communists, unless the government grants farmers advance payments for the 1997 grain harvest within a week.

"If this does not take place by August 12, the parliamentary caucus of the Polish Peasant Party will take actions aimed at dismissing Premier Cimoszewicz," PSL spokesman Aleksander Benkowski told the public television.

The threat, which came nearly seven weeks before the parliamentary general election, followed a conflict between Cimoszewicz and Peasants' Agriculture Minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski at Tuesday's cabinet meeting.

Kalinowski walked out of the meeting, when the prime minister refused to discuss his motion to let the Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), the food market regulator, pay farmers in advance for grains they would sell it later this year.
PSL's Bentkowski said his party was unlikely to leave the coalition, which had survived repeated quarrels since its creation in 1993, but would only seek to replace the prime minister.

Earlier on Tuesday Kalinowski told an urgenly called news conference that Cimoszewicz did not understand the importance of the advance payments for the farmers, which are needed to stabilise grain prices.
Leaders of the Peasant party, supported mainly by the rural electorate, later called an extraordinary meeting to decide how to react to the snag.

Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said the cabinet could not debate the advance payments for farmers because the agriculture minister had failed to present a detailed report on the food market after July's floods.
"After a presentation (of the report) the government will return to considering the advance payments," she said in a statement.

Kalinowski said that the ARR agency would need the finance minister's approval to borrow 120 million zlotys to begin granting the advances, because its funds had been reduced by aid it had extended to farmers hit the flood.

The Peasants and the opposition do not have two-thirds majority needed to dismiss Cimoszewicz in a parliamentary no-confidence vote but they could obstruct works of the government to press for his dismissal.

The PSL has suggested that after the elections it was ready to either to stay with the ex-communists in the coalition or form a new one with the opposition Solidarity Elections Action (AWS) alliance. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
